lines.text: The researchers set out to measure the length of, well, our attention spans.
On average, users stuck with a single task for 40 seconds,
down from 75 seconds measured just five years earlier.
This doesn't necessarily mean our attention spans are fundamentally getting shorter,
rather, in today's world, our attention is being pulled in more directions than ever before.
Our brains are constantly receiving a flood of information,
from sensory input to environmental cues to internal thoughts.
Filtering through it all relies on several brain regions.
The challenge of sustained attention is keeping that flashlight focused in one place.
This ability to constantly scan our environments and quickly refocus was key for human survival,
so while frustrating, getting distracted is inevitable.
But no matter your starting point, there are ways to improve your ability to stay focused.
First, tasks that appropriately challenge you tend to hold your attention best.
